# bbs.dbhq.uk

> A bulletin board system that fronts the live web. Web pages are stripped of
> script, tracking and layout, then redrawn as 16-colour CP437 text on an
> 80-column screen. Photographs are converted to ANSI art in the browser.

## What it does

- **Renders web pages as text mode.** The HTML a server sends is read for its
  landmarks and headings; nothing the page ships is executed. Pages built
  entirely with JavaScript come back empty, and that is reported rather than
  hidden.
- **Converts images to ANSI and ASCII art.** Glyph, foreground and background
  are chosen together per cell and scored against the original in a perceptual
  colour space. Sixteen colours are chosen per image from the 262,144 a VGA
  card could produce, which is what the XBIN format was for.
- **Displays classic .ANS art**, including the SAUCE record naming the artist.

## How it is built

- Rust compiled to WebAssembly. All rendering happens on the reader's machine.
- A Cloudflare Worker relays page fetches, because a browser cannot request
  another origin directly. It returns bytes and never decides how anything
  looks.
- Source: https://github.com/dbhq-uk/bbs

## Honest limits

- Roughly 70% of a fifty-page corpus of real websites renders readably; the
  measurement is published at
  https://github.com/dbhq-uk/bbs/blob/main/corpus/REPORT.md
- Single-page applications that build themselves with JavaScript do not work,
  by design.
- Small text in screenshots does not survive the conversion. That is a
  resolution limit, not a defect.
